items.text: Children count by tens and write the missing numbers in a row of tens; the same lesson also counts by fives and by twos.

lessons.title: Count to 100 on the hundreds chart

lessons.unitTitle: The Hundreds Chart and Skip Counting
lessons.title: Count by tens, fives, and twos

items.text: Children count along a number strip to 10 and to 20 and write the numbers that are missing.
Children write the numerals 0 to 9, write how many pictures they counted, and fill in the missing numbers on a number strip to 20.

lessons.title: Count and write how many: up to 20

items.text: Children give each object exactly one partner by drawing a line, and say whether there are enough.
Children count two groups of the same kind of object, one in a row and one spread out, write how many are in each, and decide whether both groups have the same number.
Children count a group of up to 9 pictures, draw one more or cross one out as the label says, and write how many there are now.
Children count a group of up to 10 pictures to tell how many there are, and color or draw a group to match a given number.

lessons.title: Make a group of that many
Count and write how many: up to 20

items.text: Children match the pictures in two rows one-to-one and say which row has more, which has fewer, or that both rows have the same number.

lessons.title: Match them up: more, fewer, or the same

items.text: Children compare two written numbers from 1 to 10 and color the greater one.
Children put two groups together, count all of them, and write how many there are in all.

lessons.title: Take away: how many are left?

items.text: Children join two groups or take some away, with totals up to 10, and write how many there are in all or how many are left.

lessons.title: Take away: how many are left?

items.text: Children break a number up to 10 into two parts and find the part that is missing in a number bond.
Children find the partner that makes 10 with a given number in a number bond, and say the pair, such as 8 and 2.
Children solve addition and subtraction facts and color each part of a picture with the color for its answer.

groups.title: Number and Operations in Base Ten

items.text: Children count a group of 11 to 19 objects, circle ten of them, and write the number as ten and some more ones, such as 10 + 4 = 14.

lessons.title: Build and draw a teen number

items.text: Children hold a real object, such as a book, a cup, or a block, and say what can be measured about it: how long it is, how heavy it is, or how much it holds.
Children compare the pictures in a row and circle the biggest or the tallest one.

lessons.unitTitle: Sorting, Tallies, and the Days of the Week
lessons.title: Which is heavier?

items.text: Children look at a mixed group of pictures, count each kind separately, and write how many of each there are.

lessons.unitTitle: Sorting, Tallies, and the Days of the Week
lessons.title: Count each kind

items.text: Children use the words on, under, beside, left, and right to say where something is, and circle the picture in the place that is named.
Children name circles, squares, triangles, and rectangles, even when a shape is turned, long, or thin.

lessons.title: What makes a shape that shape?

items.text: Children sort shapes into flat (two-dimensional) shapes and solid (three-dimensional) shapes.
Children count the sides of a shape, write the number, and match shapes to their number of sides.
Children draw named flat shapes on dot paper, joining dots so that each shape has the right number of sides and corners.
Children put tangram pieces together to make a figure and show where the pieces meet inside a shape.

pages.metaDescription: Second grade ELAR TEKS checklist for Texas: the reading and language arts expectations, the lessons and worksheets that teach them, and the ones we do not cover yet.

items.text: Children build on what others say in a book talk by linking their comments to what others said.

items.text: Children tell short from long vowels when they read regularly spelled one-syllable words (hop and hope, step and steep, ran and rain) and sort printed words by the vowel sound.
Children read and spell one-syllable words with the vowel teams ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, and ow, and choose the team for a word: first by its vowel sound, then by its place in the word.

items.text: Children split two-syllable words that have a long vowel in one syllable (rainbow, cupcake, paper), read each syllable, and read the words in sentences.
